# DESCENT RALLY

A cel-shaded downhill rally game: four procedural rally cars racing point to point from an alpine summit to the valley floor. Built with Three.js, TypeScript, Vite and Web Audio.

**Every asset is generated by this repository.** There are no downloaded cars, textures, HDRIs, fonts or sound files. Bodywork, wheels, cockpit drivers, terrain, foliage, course furniture, textures and audio are constructed in code.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the URL Vite prints and race.

---

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| **W** / **↑** | Accelerate |
| **A D** / **← →** | Steer |
| **S** / **↓** | Handbrake — release rear grip and rotate the car |
| **Q** | Foot brake — stronger, more stable braking |
| **Space** | Load the suspension; release at a crest for extra lift |
| **J / K** | Trim nose-up / nose-down attitude in the air |
| **Shift** or **E** + direction | Airborne roll correction |
| **F** | Boost — charged by controlled slides and clean landings |
| **R** | Reset to the last checkpoint |
| **C** | Look back |
| **V** | Cycle camera |
| **Esc** | Pause |
| **`** | Debug overlay |

A standard gamepad works too. The left stick bypasses keyboard smoothing.

### Rally handling

The car is not a cosmetic shell around the old bicycle. Gameplay now runs through a dedicated four-wheel arcade rally model:

- progressive steering that loses angle, not authority, at high speed
- surface-dependent lateral grip and rolling resistance
- retained lateral momentum for controllable Scandinavian-flick slides
- a rear-brake grip release instead of an instant scripted drift
- sprung body roll, brake dive, acceleration squat and independent axle compression
- terrain-tangent gravity, aerodynamic drag, crests, jumps and landing alignment
- physical crashes followed by an automatic recovery state
- boost earned through driving rather than BMX trick vocabulary

The public `IBike`/`BikeState` names remain in a few shared contracts because replay, ghost, camera, effects and AI were already built against that stable seam. The gameplay factory behind that seam now creates `RallyCarPhysics`, `RallyCarVisual` and `RallyDriverRig` instances exclusively.

---

## Art direction

The committed palette remains **dawn-gold alpine**: warm low sun, violet-slate shadows and teal atmospheric layers. The rally conversion keeps the original project’s strongest feature intact—a unified NPR pipeline rather than a toon material applied only to hero objects.

Every car part participates in the same rendering system as the mountain:

- 3–4 hard lighting bands with material-specific thresholds
- chromatic shadow bands and restrained hatch texture
- hard-edged specular shapes and generated matcap reflections
- Fresnel separation around bodywork, helmets, glass and wheels
- prepared smooth-normal inverted hulls with curvature-weighted line thickness
- screen-space normal/depth/material-ID Sobel lines for interior panel breaks
- quantised atmospheric fog, generated LUT grading and hard-threshold bloom

The rally body is assembled entirely from prepared geometry primitives: a wide lower shell, cabin, hood, roof, flared arches, side skirts, skid plate, bumpers, mirrors, lamp pod, roof scoop, rear wing, twin exhausts, four animated wheels and a bold procedural livery stripe. Four race identities reuse the authored palette instead of introducing unrelated colours.

The cockpit driver is intentionally economical. Through the glass, the readable shapes are the helmet, visor, shoulders, gloves and steering wheel. The rig looks through corners, counteracts chassis roll, follows suspension impacts and remains seated during crashes without spending the frame budget on an exposed full-body character the camera no longer needs.

---

## The mountain and course

The 4 km world begins as layered procedural noise and then runs through hydraulic and thermal erosion. Altitude, slope and erosion assign hard-edged grass, dirt, rock, scree, snow and wet-rock zones. Terrain is rendered as a geometry clipmap with snapped rings and inter-level morphing.

The 3.3 km downhill route retains nine paced sections:

1. technical exposed-rock start
2. open scree run
3. bermed forest switchbacks
4. broken rock garden
5. tabletop crest
6. ravine gap
7. exposed ridge sprint
8. wet stream bed
9. valley finish sprint

Checkpoints, split timing, wrong-way detection, corner preview, rubber-banded but fallible opponents, replay and saved best-run ghost all remain active.

## Architecture

```text
src/
  core/        fixed-step engine, input, math, RNG and noise
  npr/         palette, cel materials, line work, shadows, post pipeline and LUT
  terrain/     heightfield, erosion, zones, clipmap, scatter and foliage
  track/       spline, ribbon, checkpoints and furniture
  rally/       rally physics, procedural car visual and cockpit driver
  bike/        stable vehicle seam plus legacy low-level BMX tooling exports
  rider/       gameplay driver factory plus legacy model-viewer rig
  ai/          opponents, personalities, race director, ghost and replay
  fx/          camera, dust, debris, speed lines and impact frames
  hud/         hand-drawn canvas HUD, widgets, menus and vector typeface
  audio/       generated Web Audio synthesis
  game/        shared contracts, world constants and orchestration
tools/
  capture/     deterministic Playwright still and motion review harness
```

Physics runs at a fixed 120 Hz and rendering interpolates between steps. The new rally model allocates its vectors, quaternions, matrices and terrain samples once, outside the update path. Visual geometry is cached and shared across all four cars; only identity materials and scene hierarchies are per racer.

---

## Review harness

```bash
npm run capture:install
node tools/capture/capture.mjs --poses
node tools/capture/capture.mjs --seq pack-race --frames 60
```

The harness takes control of the simulation clock and produces deterministic retina stills, frame sequences and contact sheets. The rally branch also includes a GitHub Actions review gate that runs:

1. GLSL validation
2. strict TypeScript checking
3. the Vite production build
4. a Chromium close-up capture
5. a short pack-race motion capture

This catches shader, integration and presentation regressions before the branch is merged.

---

## Performance target

Target hardware remains a MacBook Pro-class machine in Chrome at a locked 60 fps with adaptive retina resolution.

- terrain clipmap and aggressive frustum culling
- instanced foliage, rocks, dust and debris
- cached shared rally geometry
- reduced-detail opponent cars
- no external asset decoding or network fetches
- allocation-free rally physics updates
- adaptive render scale with fast drop and slow recovery
- HUD redraws limited to changed canvas regions

Run `npm run build` for the same TypeScript, shader and production-bundle gate used by CI.
